title: Edge queue hysteresis and fast-reconnect shim to reduce 5xx/timeouts during tenant surges
creator: Anita Singh
description:
Summary: During recent customer escalations we observed correlated 5xx spikes and long tail timeouts originating at the edge layer when high-traffic tenants reconnected after maintenance windows. Root cause analysis showed an interplay of: (1) a bursty reconnection pattern from SDK clients after transient network restores, (2) edge proxy admission logic opening many downstream connections simultaneously (no hysteresis), and (3) connection keepalive/idle thresholds that caused head-of-line stalls in upstream connection pools. The result was request queue buildup, increased KV-cache churn on workers, and amplified retry storms leading to 502/504 responses for downstream customers.

Mitigation implemented so far: deployed an emergency circuit at the edge that enforces a per-tenant admission window (token-bucket) plus a soft-hysteresis delay when re-opening a previously drained connection pool. Adjusted keepalive from 90s to 30s for affected routes to reduce stale connection accumulation. Added a short-lived shim that gracefully rejects the thundering-herd reconnections with 429+Retry-After for non-priority tenants to break retry amplification. These changes are behind a runtime feature-flag and active in US region edges for 10% of the traffic (canary).

Planned permanent fix: implement a server-side 'fast-reconnect shim' that: (a) detects reconnection storms by measuring per-tenant reconnection rate over a 10s sliding window, (b) applies progressive admission control and per-tenant backoff hints, (c) integrates with the circuit-breaker to prefer healthy routes/model-variants rather than immediate retries, and (d) exposes clear SDK guidance for exponential backoff with jitter and idempotency tokens. We'll also tune proxy semaphore counts and upstream pool size to match observed steady-state inflight per-GPU capacity.

Testing and rollout: unit and integration tests added for token-bucket logic and hysteresis timers. Staging canary with synthetic tenant replay shows a 74% reduction in 5xx spikes and a 45% lower retry-amplification-rate. Rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with manual gate checks at each step. Monitoring gates: per-tenant error-rate, global 5xx rate, inflight queue length, KV-cache eviction rate, and SLA error budget. If any gate exceeds threshold we automatically rollback the feature flag.

Observability additions: new metrics exported: edge.per_tenant.reconnect_rate, edge.per_tenant.admission_denied, edge.pool.idle_count, edge.pool.acquired_latency_ms, edge.retry_amplification_ratio. Dashboards created in Console under "Edge Reconnections" and alert rules added for sustained reconnect_rate > 200 reqs/min per tenant. Added a tracing tag (edge.reconnect_cause) to correlate SDK client version and route.

Customer comms and incident handling: created a targeted customer communication template (link below) and a runbook for SREs to temporarily escalate tenant priority or open rate-limited fastpaths for strategic customers. We coordinated with Support to notify the 3 highest-impact tenants and offered migration to a Dedicated pool if needed.

Links: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/edge-fast-reconnect-shim (draft); Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosted-api/edge-reconnect-runbook; Postmortem: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-09-edge-reconnect-postmortem; Customer email template: https://docs.redwood.ai/comms/customer-reconnect-template

Next steps: (1) complete code review and merge PR, (2) expand canary to 20% and validate metrics for 6 hours, (3) coordinate SDK team to publish backoff guidelines and optional client-side jitter change, (4) finalize performance tuning on proxy semaphores and release as runtime-1.22, (5) follow-up action to instrument per-tenant SLA rollback triggers and automate tiered fastpath handling.
